campaign.instructions: Use the six R2 references as a coherent campaign visual grammar: bright white, soft blue and navy; neutral daylight; soft grounded shadows; photographic material depth and a credible shared material world. Strong blue/navy headline, readable secondary text and stable official logo/category/sequence treatment. Integrate relationship diagrams into the same physical scene, with matching light, material and depth; a flat standalone white infographic alone does not establish the chosen R2 family. Vary view angle, scene scale, negative space and scene/diagram balance according to each card reader question or action. Fabless Planning scenes should express product, plan and outsourced-lot relationships; Partner Architecture scenes should express ownership, handoff, reconciliation and responsibility. Semiconductor cues must suit the cohort; never require OSAT chip trays for Fabless or Partner. Maintain identity and hierarchy across both complete five-card carousels while each card adds a distinct meaning. Support opening orientation, comparison, context, responsibility/next step and closing as a flexible narrative, not a mandatory universal workflow. Keep closing/source content clearly separated and readable at ordinary desktop and 390px mobile viewing scale without zoom. Preserve reviewed Taiwan attribution and source scope; do not imply a facility or deployment. Transfer only reviewed colors, lighting, shadows, material depth, typography hierarchy, campaign identity and scene-integrated diagram language. Never copy reference words, record values, exact composition or a fixed prop list; no 12/38/50 layout requirement, mandatory paper/pen/tray, five-folder count or Taipei skyline. Print only exact approved artwork fields/labels and the official mark; caption/native headline/alt stay outside raster. Diagrams may use only reviewed labels, with no invented identifiers dates metrics statuses guarantees or outcomes. Do not add internal proof/review caveats or technical instructions as viewer wording. Actual images must be judged per card, full five-card narrative and across scenarios; unique prompts, IDs, hashes or prop counts cannot prove visual quality.
